Analysis Pipeline for "Multimodal Characteristics of Phase Transitions in Collaborative Conversation"

James Trujillo & Travis Wiltshire

Info documents

This analysis pipeline covers the main data processing for the "Multimodal Characteristics of Phase Transitions in Collaborative Conversation" paper. The notebook covers all processing and statistical analysis steps except for the information content calculation.
This pipeline is running in Python 3.12.4.

This pipeline is adapted from the Analyzing Multi-Party Turn-Taking Behavior EnvisionBOX module that used the same dataset and provided the initial exploration of the turn-taking entropy analyses:
Trujillo, J.P. (2024-04-23). Analyzing Multi-Party Turn-Taking Behavior . Retrieved from: https://envisionbox.org/turntaking_entropy.html

Data Processing and Preparation¶

The first code blocks do the initial module imports and function definitions for calculating the turn-transition timing data from the transcripts.

def get_multispeaker_transitions(utterances_1, utterances_2, utterances_3):
    # set max distance between them to be 2s, then find the closest occurence in
    # second dataframe. Max distance is based on Heldner & Edlund 2010
    # output times are in ms
    
    speaker_count = 3
    if not utterances_1:
        speaker_count -=1
    if not utterances_2:
        speaker_count -=1
    if not utterances_3:
        speaker_count -=1
    
    if speaker_count < 2: 
        trans_dur = np.nan
        gap_dur = np.nan
        utterance_time_trans = np.nan
        utterance_time_gap = np.nan
    else:
        trans_dur1, gap_dur1, utterance_time_trans1, utterance_time_gap1, overlap_dur1, utterance_time_overlap1,timestamp1 = get_gaps_overlaps(
          utterances_1, utterances_2, utterances_3)
        trans_dur2, gap_dur2, utterance_time_trans2, utterance_time_gap2, overlap_dur2, utterance_time_overlap2,timestamp2 = get_gaps_overlaps(
          utterances_2, utterances_1, utterances_3) 
        trans_dur3, gap_dur3, utterance_time_trans3, utterance_time_gap3, overlap_dur3, utterance_time_overlap3,timestamp3 = get_gaps_overlaps(
          utterances_3, utterances_2, utterances_1) 
        
        
        # these will be used in the dataframe to indicate which speaker we're talking about
        p1 = ["1"]*len(trans_dur1)
        p2 = ["2"]*len(trans_dur2)
        p3 = ["3"]*len(trans_dur3)
        
        participant = p1 + p2 + p3
        timestamp = timestamp1 + timestamp2 + timestamp3

        # now we need to stack the utterance data
        trans_dur = trans_dur1 + trans_dur2 + trans_dur3
        utterance_time_trans = utterance_time_trans1 + utterance_time_trans2 + utterance_time_trans3
        
        df = pd.DataFrame(np.column_stack([participant,timestamp,trans_dur, utterance_time_trans]),
                               columns=['participant', 'timestamp','transition_duration','utterance_duration']
                               )
        
        return df
        
        
def get_gaps_overlaps(utterances_1, utterances_2, utterances_3):
    # this gets the utterance and turn-transition speaker from the perspective of one speaker
    # It doesn't matter what order the second two are in, as we just care about the averages in 
    # the end anyway
    trans_dur = []
    utterance_time_trans = []
    timestamp=[]

    for u_idx,u in enumerate(utterances_1):
        # here we want to get the difference between this utterance's offset (u[1]) and all onsets from the other two speakers
        diffs2 = [abs(float(u[1]) - float(u2[0])) for u2 in utterances_2]
        diffs3 = [abs(float(u[1]) - float(u3[0])) for u3 in utterances_3]

        min_dif2 = np.argmin(diffs2)
        min_dif3 = np.argmin(diffs3)        

        # also get within-speaker differences
        # we get this to make sure our inter-speaker differences are less than this
        # otherwise, we may not be getting the turn transition from this utterance
        if u_idx < len(utterances_1)-1:
            min_pause = utterances_1[u_idx+1][0] - u[1]
        else:
            # if this is not the last utterance, we ignore this
            min_pause = min([diffs2[min_dif2],diffs3[min_dif3]]) +1
        # is there an utterance from p2 or p3 starting within 2s of this utterance from p1?

        if diffs2[min_dif2] < 2000 and diffs2[min_dif2] < min_pause:
            trans_dur.append(int(utterances_2[min_dif2][0] - u[1]))
            utterance_time_trans.append(int(utterances_1[u_idx][1] - utterances_1[u_idx][0]))
            timestamp.append(int(utterances_2[min_dif2][0]))
        if diffs3[min_dif3] < 2000 and diffs3[min_dif3] < min_pause:
            trans_dur.append(int(utterances_3[min_dif3][0] - u[1]))
            utterance_time_trans.append(int(utterances_1[u_idx][1] - utterances_1[u_idx][0]))
            timestamp.append(int(utterances_3[min_dif3][0]))
            
    # finally, we want to separate these values into gaps and overlaps
    gap_dur = []
    overlap_dur = []
    utterance_time_gap = []
    utterance_time_overlap = []
    for idx, val in enumerate(trans_dur):
        if val > 0:
            gap_dur.append(val)
            utterance_time_gap.append(int(utterance_time_trans[idx]))
        elif val <= 0:
            overlap_dur.append(val)
            utterance_time_overlap.append(int(utterance_time_trans[idx]))

    return trans_dur, gap_dur, utterance_time_trans, utterance_time_gap, overlap_dur, utterance_time_overlap,timestamp

Proper Analyses¶

Question 1: Do instability peaks predict time on task?¶

For the first RQ, we will get the speaker transcripts, remove intraspeaker transitions, then calculate turn-taking timing.

    group_entropy.append(entropy)

Next, we calculate the turn-taking entropy within each conversation, and tag the instability peaks (which we take as phase transition points)

tt_entropy_starts = []
# for each of our groups..
for group in groups:
    transcript = pd.read_csv("./transcripts/" +group + "_Oracle.csv")
    utterances_1 = transcript[transcript["Participant"] == 1]
    utterances_1_SE = [(utterance[1]["Start"]*1000,utterance[1]["End"]*1000) for utterance in utterances_1.iterrows()]
    utterances_2 = transcript[transcript["Participant"] == 2]
    utterances_2_SE = [(utterance[1]["Start"]*1000,utterance[1]["End"]*1000) for utterance in utterances_2.iterrows()]
    utterances_3 = transcript[transcript["Participant"] == 3]
    utterances_3_SE = [(utterance[1]["Start"]*1000,utterance[1]["End"]*1000) for utterance in utterances_3.iterrows()]
    
    # ..get the turn-transition dataframes..
    df_cps = get_multispeaker_transitions(utterances_1_SE, utterances_2_SE, utterances_3_SE)
    
    # .. and then calculate entropy
    # first we need to sort this into a proper timeseries, disregarding individual IDs
    df_cps.timestamp = pd.to_numeric(df_cps.timestamp, errors='coerce')
    df_cps.transition_duration = pd.to_numeric(df_cps.transition_duration, errors='coerce')

    sort_df = df_cps.sort_values(by=["timestamp"], ascending=True)
    
    tt_entropy = []
    tt_entropy_starts_local = []

    tt_density = []

    window_length = (1000*60) #written out just to make the window length easily understandable

    window_start =sort_df["timestamp"].loc[0]
    window_end =  window_start + window_length
    while window_end < sort_df["timestamp"][len(sort_df)-1]   :
        # get data for this time window
        window = sort_df[(sort_df["timestamp"] >window_start)&(sort_df["timestamp"] <window_end)]
        tt_entropy_starts_local.append(window_start)
        if len(window) > 3:
        # calculate permutation entropy
            tt_entropy.append(ant.perm_entropy(window["transition_duration"], normalize=True))
            tt_density.append(len(window["transition_duration"]))
        else:
            tt_entropy.append(np.nan)
            tt_density.append(np.nan)
        # shift the window forward by 30s
        window_start = window_end - window_length/2 
        window_end = window_start + window_length

    tt_entropy_starts.append(tt_entropy_starts_local)
    tt_entropy_full.append(tt_entropy)
    instability_peaks, instability_prominence = signal.find_peaks(tt_entropy, height=.4, prominence=0.2, distance=2)

    group_list_check.append(group)
    group_instability_peaks.append(len(instability_peaks))
    group_instability_peaks_idx.append(instability_peaks)
    group_instability_peak_prom.append(instability_prominence["peak_heights"])
    group_instability_mag.append(np.mean(instability_prominence["peak_heights"]))
    group_instability_prom.append(np.mean(instability_prominence["prominences"]))
    group_tt_density.append(tt_density)

time_on_task = []

for group in groups:

    ToT = transcript["End"].iloc[-1]
    time_on_task.append(ToT)
    
df_cps_full["ToT"] = time_on_task

In team-based problem-solving tasks, moments of critical instability may be necessary changes in the dynamic of a conversation/discussion, where a team is (for example) changing strategies or trying to find a stable dynamic. Accordingly, many such changes in dynamics are likely to be associated with a longer time working on a problem. Teams that find a stable, effective dynamic with fewer such changes, will then be faster. Even without looking into what exactly is occurring during a conversation, this type of analysis can provide a first look at whether moments of critical instability are associated with how long it takes to complete a task.

This is a nice check, but instability peaks are likely to occur as time goes on, so there's likely a positive association between number of peaks and length of time-series, regardless of anything function. So we need to take the rate of peaks/phase transitions to factor this out.

def normalize_data(data):
    normed_data = (data-np.nanmin(data))/(np.nanmax(data)-np.nanmin(data)) 
    return normed_data

Research Question 2:What multimodal communication characteristics (linguistic, gestural) precede an upcoming phase transition?¶

RQ2 a: Semantic Flow¶

Here, we'll use the Flow Score (basically, semantic influence) to quantify the flow of information, or semantic coupling, between speaking turns. The main question here is: are moments of critical instability preceded by, or followed by, changes in semantic flow?
This is based on Burdisso, 2024's DSE (as implemented in Dialog2Flow) model (https://huggingface.co/sergioburdisso/dialog2flow-joint-dse-base).
What this is actually doing is calculating the semantic similarity between each pair of consecutive turns. The model is trained on dialogue data, so it should have a better representation of turn-to-turn similarity than, for example, a more basic word embedding model that is just treating each utterance as an independent bag of words.

First, we need to load the model. Then, preprocess the transcripts a bit. Then, we calculate Flow.

NOTE: the semantic flow values have been saved to a pickle container, so the next few code blocks can be skipped in order to not re-run the model

from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel import torch from numpy import dot from numpy.linalg import norm #Mean Pooling - Take attention mask into account for correct averaging def mean_pooling(model_output, attention_mask): token_embeddings = model_output[0] #First element of model_output contains all token embeddings input_mask_expanded = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand(token_embeddings.size()).float() return torch.sum(token_embeddings * input_mask_expanded, 1) / torch.clamp(input_mask_expanded.sum(1), min=1e-9) def cosine_similarity(a,b): cos_sim = dot(a, b)/(norm(a)*norm(b)) return cos_sim # Sentences we want sentence embeddings for #sentences = ['your phone please', 'okay may i have your telephone number please'] #sentences = ['What do we do next', 'okay may i have your telephone number please'] #sentences = ['What do we do next', 'We can try this other thing'] # Load model from HuggingFace Hub tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('sergioburdisso/dialog2flow-joint-dse-base') model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('sergioburdisso/dialog2flow-joint-dse-base')

First, we need to preprocess the utterances, similarly to above, but now maintaining the transcript utterances, while removing intraspeaker gaps.

CPS = pd.read_csv("./annotations/All_Groups_CPS.csv") # first get the unique group IDs groups = list(set(CPS["Group"])) groups.sort() df_full = [] for group in groups: utterance = [] start_time = [] end_time = [] speaker = [] transcript = pd.read_csv("./transcripts/" + group + "_Oracle.csv") current_speaker = transcript["Participant"][0] current_utterance = transcript["Transcript"][0] current_start = transcript["Start"][0] current_end = transcript["End"][0] for index, row in transcript.iterrows(): if index > 0: if row["Participant"] == current_speaker or index == len(transcript)<1: extension = " " + row["Transcript"] current_utterance += extension current_end = row["End"] else: utterance.append(current_utterance) start_time.append(current_start) speaker.append(current_speaker) end_time.append(current_end) current_speaker = row["Participant"] current_utterance = row["Transcript"] current_start = row["Start"] current_end = row["End"] df_group = pd.DataFrame(np.column_stack([start_time, end_time, speaker, utterance]), columns=["start","end", "speaker", "utterance"], ) df_full.append(df_group) CPS = pd.read_csv("./annotations/All_Groups_CPS.csv") # Now we can encode, calculate similarity, calculate entropy

sim_full = [] for df_group in df_full: sim_list = [] start_list = [] sentences = list(df_group["utterance"]) #Tokenize sentences encoded_input = tokenizer(sentences, padding=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt') # Compute token embeddings with torch.no_grad(): model_output = model(**encoded_input) # Perform pooling. In this case, mean pooling. sentence_embeddings = mean_pooling(model_output, encoded_input['attention_mask']) for index in range(1,len(sentence_embeddings)): sim = cosine_similarity(sentence_embeddings[index-1],sentence_embeddings[index]) sim_list.append(sim) start_list.append(df_group["start"][index-1]) sim_full.append((start_list, sim_list)) with open('semantic_flow.pickle', 'wb') as handle: pickle.dump(sim_full, handle, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)

After all this, we can calculate entropy using the same sliding time-window approach as we did for turn-taking, and bring together with turn-taking data to visualize how the patterns line up.

In [19]:
import antropy as ant
import scipy.stats
In [20]:
sim_entropy_full = []
sim_entropy_starts_full = []

sim_group = []
sim_window = []
sim_entropy_val = []
similarity = []


# for each of our groups..
group_idx = 0
for group in sim_full:

    timestamps = [float(val) for val in group[0]]
    sim_scores = [float(val) for val in group[1]]
    
    # .. and then calculate entropy
    sim_entropy = []
    sim_entropy_starts_local = []
    
    window_length = 60 #written out just to make the window length easily understandable

    window_start = 0
    #window_start = float(timestamps[0])
    window_end =  window_start + window_length
    
    window_idx = 0
    while window_end < timestamps[len(timestamps)-1]:
        sim_entropy_starts_local.append(window_start)
        # get data for this time window
        
        window_indices = [idx for idx,x in enumerate(timestamps) if (timestamps[idx] >= window_start) & (timestamps[idx] < window_end)]
        window = [sim_scores[idx] for idx in window_indices]
        
        if len(window) > 3:
        # calculate permutation entropy
            val = ant.perm_entropy(window, normalize=True)
            sim_entropy.append(val)
            sim_entropy_val.append(val)
            similarity.append(np.mean(window))
        else:
            sim_entropy.append(np.nan)
            sim_entropy_val.append(np.nan)
            similarity.append(np.nan)

        sim_group.append(group_idx)
        sim_window.append(window_idx)
        

        # shift the window forward by 15s
        window_start = window_end - window_length/2 
        window_end = window_start + window_length
        window_idx += 1
    
    sim_entropy_full.append(sim_entropy)
    sim_entropy_starts_full.append(sim_entropy_starts_local)

    group_idx +=1


sim_df = pd.DataFrame(np.column_stack([sim_group, sim_window, similarity, sim_entropy_val]),
                      columns=["group","window","sem_similarity", "sem_entropy"])

Next, we formally test whether semantic entropy close to the TT entropy peaks is different from baseline.

RQ2a Statistical Testing: is semantic flow immediately before phase transition different than average?
The hypothesis here is that semantic flow will be lower, representing divergence immediately before a transition. The method: 1) calculate the global mean of semantic flow for each group, 2) take a 2min window before each instability peak, 3) calculate mean semantic flow within this window, 4) use mixed regression to test difference from group mean.
Basically, we're testing if the semantic entropy immediately before or after a turn-taking instability peak are higher than the average semantic entropy for that particular group.

In [25]:
def fwhm2std(fwhm):
    """from fwhm to standard deviation of a gaussian"""
    return fwhm/2.355

def smoothing(data, window_size=5):
    data = pd.Series(data).interpolate(method="spline",order=2)
    
    #window_size = 5
    
    std = fwhm2std(window_size)
    smoothed_time_series = data.rolling(window_size, win_type="gaussian", center=True).mean(std=std)

    return smoothed_time_series

def calc_ci(data):

    data_int = pd.Series(data).interpolate(method="spline",order=2)
    
    ci = scipy.stats.t.interval(confidence=0.99, df=len(data_int)-1, 
                                loc=np.mean(data_int), 
                                scale=scipy.stats.sem(data_int, nan_policy="omit")) 
    
    return ci

Below, I'm testing out some interpolation and smoothing parameters. This is because in order to calculate confidence intervals, which are required for RQ3, we need a complete time-series. The jagged, raw entropy values also do not seem handy for this, even if it's possible to ignore the NAs. So, following Stening et al., 2023, we're using a Gaussian kernel to smooth the data.

def fwhm2std(fwhm):
    """from fwhm to standard deviation of a gaussian"""
    return fwhm/2.355

def smoothing(data, window_size=5):
    data = pd.Series(data).interpolate(method="spline",order=2)
    
    #window_size = 5
    
    std = fwhm2std(window_size)
    smoothed_time_series = data.rolling(window_size, win_type="gaussian", center=True).mean(std=std)

    return smoothed_time_series

import random

def generate_pseudo_df():
    lead_values = []
    follow_values = []
    group_list = []
    peak_list = []
    lead_diff_values = []
    follow_diff_values = []
    
    group_means = []
    
    for group in range(len(tt_entropy_full)):
        current_peaks = group_instability_peaks_idx[group]
        current_sim_entropy = sim_entropy_full[group]
    
        group_means.append(np.nanmean(sim_entropy_full[group]))
    
        peak_idx = 0
        for peak in current_peaks:
            pseudo_peak = random.randint(5,len(current_sim_entropy)-5)
            # take the preceding 4 data points
            lead_sim = current_sim_entropy[pseudo_peak-4:pseudo_peak]
            follow_sim = current_sim_entropy[pseudo_peak+1:pseudo_peak+5]
            lead_values.extend(lead_sim)
            follow_values.extend(follow_sim)

            follow_diff_values.extend([val-group_means[group] for val in follow_sim])
            lead_diff_values.extend([val-group_means[group] for val in lead_sim])
            
            group_list.extend([group]*len(lead_sim))
            peak_list.extend([peak_idx]*len(lead_sim))
    
            peak_idx+=1
    
    df_entropy_pseudo = pd.DataFrame(np.column_stack([group_list, peak_list, lead_diff_values, follow_diff_values]),
                                   columns=["group","peak", "lead", "follow"],
                                   )
    return df_entropy_pseudo

gesture_annot_files = sorted([filename for filename in os.listdir("./annotations/") if "GAMR" in filename and filename.endswith(".eaf")])

def get_window_of_annotations(eafob, group,start_time, end_time):
    # requires a bit of exception handling due to somevariability in naming conventions
    if "Tier-1" in eafob.get_tier_names():
        gesture_annots = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Tier-1", start_time, end_time)]
    else:
        try:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 1", start_time, end_time)]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 2", start_time, end_time)]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 3", start_time, end_time)]
        except KeyError:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_1", start_time, end_time)]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_2", start_time, end_time)]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_3", start_time, end_time)]
        gesture_annots = g_1 + g_2 + g_3

    return gesture_annots


def get_gesture_annotations(eafob):

    if "Tier-1" in eafob.get_tier_names():
        gesture_annots = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Tier-1")]
    else:
        try:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Participant 1")]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Participant 2")]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Participant 3")]
        except KeyError:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Participant_1")]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Participant_2")]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_for_tier("Participant_3")]
        gesture_annots = g_1 + g_2 + g_3

    return gesture_annots


def get_video_dur(group):
    if group <10:
        transcript = pd.read_csv("./transcripts/Group_0" + str(group) + "_Oracle.csv")
    else:
        transcript = pd.read_csv("./transcripts/Group_" + str(group) + "_Oracle.csv")
    final = transcript["End"][len(transcript)-1]

    return final

}

    g_df[list(window_cols.values())]
    .rename(columns={col: position for position, col in window_cols.items()})
    .melt(var_name="window", value_name="gesture_count")
)

summary = (
    plot_df
    .groupby("window")["gesture_count"]
    .agg(mean="mean", n="count", sd="std")
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values("window")
)

summary["sem"] = summary["sd"] / np.sqrt(summary["n"])
summary["ci_95"] = summary.apply(
    lambda row: stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=row["n"] - 1) * row["sem"]
    if row["n"] > 1 else np.nan,
    axis=1
)

# Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))

ax.errorbar(
    summary["window"],
    summary["mean"],
    yerr=summary["ci_95"],
    fmt="-o",
    capsize=5,
    linewidth=2,
    markersize=7,
    color="#2C7FB8",
    ecolor="#2C7FB8"
)

# Mark the point separating pre-peak and post-peak windows
ax.axvline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
ax.text(0, ax.get_ylim()[1], "Peak", ha="center", va="bottom")

ax.set_xticks(summary["window"])
ax.set_xticklabels([
    "−4", "−3", "−2", "−1",
    "+1", "+2", "+3", "+4"
])

ax.set_xlabel("Window relative to peak")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean gesture count per window")
ax.set_title("Gesture counts before and after instability peaks")

ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Temporal ordering of the gesture-count windows
window_cols = {
    -4: "lead_gesture_count_4",
    -3: "lead_gesture_count_3",
    -2: "lead_gesture_count_2",
    -1: "lead_gesture_count",
     1: "follow_gesture_count",
     2: "follow_gesture_count_2",
     3: "follow_gesture_count_3",
     4: "follow_gesture_count_4",
}

# Convert from wide to long format
plot_df = (
    g_df[["group", "peak_id", "group_gesture_rate", *window_cols.values()]]
    .rename(columns={col: window for window, col in window_cols.items()})
    .melt(
        id_vars=["group", "peak_id", "group_gesture_rate"],
        var_name="window",
        value_name="gesture_count"
    )
)

plot_df["window"] = pd.to_numeric(plot_df["window"])
plot_df["gesture_count"] = pd.to_numeric(plot_df["gesture_count"], errors="coerce")
plot_df["group_gesture_rate"] = pd.to_numeric(
    plot_df["group_gesture_rate"], errors="coerce"
)

# As requested:
# positive values = more gestures in this window than the group's average
# negative values = fewer gestures in this window than the group's average
plot_df["difference_from_group_average"] = (
    plot_df["gesture_count"] - plot_df["group_gesture_rate"]
)

# Average across peaks within each group and time window,
# with 95% confidence intervals across peaks
summary = (
    plot_df
    .groupby(["group", "window"])["difference_from_group_average"]
    .agg(mean="mean", n="count", sd="std")
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values(["group", "window"])
)

summary["sem"] = summary["sd"] / np.sqrt(summary["n"])
summary["ci_95"] = summary.apply(
    lambda row: (
        stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=row["n"] - 1) * row["sem"]
        if row["n"] > 1 else np.nan
    ),
    axis=1
)

# Plot one line per group
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))

groups = sorted(summary["group"].unique())
colours = plt.cm.tab20(np.linspace(0, 1, len(groups)))

for group, colour in zip(groups, colours):
    group_data = summary[summary["group"] == group]

    ax.errorbar(
        group_data["window"],
        group_data["mean"],
        yerr=group_data["ci_95"],
        fmt="-o",
        capsize=3,
        linewidth=1.5,
        markersize=4,
        color=colour,
        alpha=0.85,
        label=f"Group {group}"
    )

# Reference lines
ax.axvline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linestyle=":", linewidth=1)

ax.set_xticks([-4, -3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3, 4])
ax.set_xticklabels(["−4", "−3", "−2", "−1", "+1", "+2", "+3", "+4"])

ax.set_xlabel("Window relative to instability peak")
ax.set_ylabel("gesture count - Group average gesture rate")
ax.set_title("Gesture-count deviation from each group's average")

ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

# Put the potentially long group legend outside the plot
ax.legend(
    title="Group",
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc="upper left",
    borderaxespad=0
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

def get_window_of_annotations(eafob, group,start_time, end_time):
    # requires a bit of exception handling due to somevariability in naming conventions
    if "Tier-1" in eafob.get_tier_names():
        gesture_annots = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Tier-1", start_time, end_time)]
    else:
        try:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 1", start_time, end_time)]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 2", start_time, end_time)]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 3", start_time, end_time)]
        except KeyError:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_1", start_time, end_time)]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_2", start_time, end_time)]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_3", start_time, end_time)]
        gesture_annots = g_1 + g_2 + g_3

    return gesture_annots

            gesture_annots_lead = get_window_of_annotations(eafob, group+1,start_time, end_time)

    #print(lead_gesture_list)
    g_df_pseudo = pd.DataFrame(list(zip(group_list, peak_idx_list, lead_gesture_list, lead_gest_rate_list,
                                follow_gesture_list, follow_gest_rate_list)),
                        columns=["group", "peak_id", 
                                 "lead_gesture_count", "lead_gesture_rate",
                                "follow_gesture_count", "follow_gesture_rate"])

    return g_df_pseudo

def get_window_of_annotations(eafob, group,start_time, end_time):
    # requires a bit of exception handling due to some variability in naming conventions
    if "Tier-1" in eafob.get_tier_names():
        gesture_annots = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Tier-1", start_time, end_time)]
    else:
        try:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 1", start_time, end_time)]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 2", start_time, end_time)]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant 3", start_time, end_time)]
        except KeyError:
            g_1 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_1", start_time, end_time)]
            g_2 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_2", start_time, end_time)]
            g_3 = [annotation for annotation in eafob.get_annotation_data_between_times("Participant_3", start_time, end_time)]
        gesture_annots = g_1 + g_2 + g_3

    return gesture_annots

        # get the CI threshold
        threshold = group_ci[group][1]

        # get the gesture coding data
        eafob = pympi.Elan.Eaf("./annotations/" + gesture_annot_files[group])
        
        if tt_entropy_smooth[group].iloc[peak_idx] > threshold:

            step_ms = window_length / 2 # 30,000 ms

            # the time-series is used to find the end of the relaxation window
            time_series = tt_entropy_smooth[group][peak_idx:]

            # number of steps after the peak to the first below-threshold bin
            relax_steps = next((x for x,y in enumerate(time_series) if y < threshold and x >0),
                           None,) # get None in case nothing is returned, so we can properly capture this 


            if relax_steps is None:
                # No below-threshold bin was found after the peak
                relax_window_dur_ms = None # duration, in milliseconds, of the relaxation period (return to baseline entropy)
                start_time = peak_idx * step_ms # the actual timestamps associated with the relaxation period
                end_time = None
                continue
            else:
                end_idx = peak_idx + relax_steps  # Position in the original binned series
            
                start_time = peak_idx * step_ms # the actual timestamps associated with the relaxation period
                end_time = end_idx * step_ms
                relax_window_dur_ms = relax_steps * step_ms # duration, in milliseconds, of the relaxation period (return to baseline entropy)
                

            gesture_annots = get_window_of_annotations(eafob, group,start_time, end_time)

                # store the data

                peak_idx_list.append(peak_idx)
                relax_dur_list.append(relax_window_dur_ms/1000)
                relax_gesture_list.append(len(gesture_annots))
                relax_gest_rate_list.append((len(gesture_annots)/(relax_window_dur_ms/1000))*60)
                deixis_count_list.append(len([gest for gest in gesture_annots if "deixis" in gest[2]]))
                emblem_count_list.append(len([gest for gest in gesture_annots if "emblem" in gest[2]]))
                iconic_count_list.append(len([gest for gest in gesture_annots if "iconic" in gest[2]]))
                sem_entropy_list.append(mean_sem_entropy)
                sem_entropy_slope_list.append(slope)
                
            
g_df = pd.DataFrame(list(zip(group_list, peak_idx_list, relax_dur_list,

RQ3b Result: There is (borderline) evidence for a positive association between information density and reorganization time¶

RQ3c: Gesture Use

This is based on the idea that gestures regulate turn-taking in some ways, and also help to communicate more generally.
In terms of reorganization, we can use Grimm's (2023) operationalization as a time to return to baseline: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/15553434231199729
Specifically, we'll use the upper bound of the 99% Confidence Interval of the data. For this to make sense, we'll first interpolate the missing data, and then smooth it.
Gesture rate during return-to-baseline window can be correlated with reorganization time.

First, we need to calculate the reorganization windows, then extract all gestures from that window.
Data:

  • the peaks are defined in group_instability_peaks_idx
  • the time-series data are in tt_entropy_full

# Function to detect outliers using Z-Score
def detect_outliers_zscore(data, threshold=2.5):

    # Step 1: Calculate mean and standard deviation of the data
    mean, std = np.mean(data), np.std(data)

    # Step 2: Compute Z-scores for each data point
    # Formula: (x - mean) / standard deviation
    z_scores = [(x - mean) / std for x in data]

    # Step 3: Identify data points where |Z-score| > threshold
    outliers = [x for x in data if abs((x - mean) / std) > threshold]

    return z_scores, outliers


# Example usage with DataFrame column "feature1"

Permutation tests: communication features during relaxation windows¶

The following tests ask whether gesture rate, information content, and semantic entropy during the observed relaxation windows differ from chance. For every observed relaxation event, each permutation samples one random window of the same duration from the same group's data. The mean of the per-group means is used as the test statistic so that groups with more instability peaks do not receive more weight.

In [77]:
relax_features_df = (
    g_df.merge(
        ic_df[["group", "peak_id", "relax_info_content"]],
        on=["group", "peak_id"],
        how="inner",
    )[
        [
            "group",
            "peak_id",
            "relax_duration",
            "gesture_rate",
            "relax_info_content",
            "mean_semantic_entropy",
        ]
    ]
)

relax_step_ms = window_length / 2
relax_group_data = {}

for group in sorted(relax_features_df["group"].unique()):
    group = int(group)
    group_str = f"{group + 1:02d}"

    transcript = pd.read_csv(f"./transcripts/Group_{group_str}_Oracle.csv")
    info_content = pd.read_csv(
        glob.glob(f"./InformationContent/context_entropy_data/Group_{group_str}*")[0]
    )
    eafob = pympi.Elan.Eaf("./annotations/" + gesture_annot_files[group])

    video_end_ms = int(transcript["End"].iloc[-1] * 1000)
    info_end_ms = int(info_content["onset"].max() * 1000)
    semantic_end_ms = int((len(sim_entropy_full[group]) - 1) * relax_step_ms)

    relax_group_data[group] = {
        "eafob": eafob,
        "info_content": info_content,
        "max_end_ms": min(video_end_ms, info_end_ms, semantic_end_ms),
    }


def relaxation_group_balanced_mean(data, value_col):
    clean = data[["group", value_col]].dropna()
    return clean.groupby("group")[value_col].mean().mean()


def report_relaxation_permutation(value_col, title, x_label):
    observed = relax_true_stat[value_col]
    null_values = np.asarray(relax_perm_stat[value_col], dtype=float)
    null_values = null_values[np.isfinite(null_values)]

    p_lower = (np.sum(null_values <= observed) + 1) / (len(null_values) + 1)
    p_upper = (np.sum(null_values >= observed) + 1) / (len(null_values) + 1)
    p_two_sided = min(1.0, 2 * min(p_lower, p_upper))

    sns.histplot(null_values, kde=True)
    plt.axvline(observed, color="red", label="Observed statistic")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.xlabel(x_label)
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

    print(f"Observed group-balanced mean: {observed:.6f}")
    print(f"Valid permutations: {len(null_values)}")
    print(f"Lower-tail p: {p_lower:.4f}")
    print(f"Upper-tail p: {p_upper:.4f}")
    print(f"Two-sided p: {p_two_sided:.4f}")
In [78]:
def generate_relaxation_pseudo_df():
    pseudo_rows = []

    for _, observed in relax_features_df.iterrows():
        group = int(observed["group"])
        duration_ms = int(round(observed["relax_duration"] * 1000))
        window_steps = int(round(duration_ms / relax_step_ms))
        semantic_points = window_steps + 1

        group_data = relax_group_data[group]
        max_start_from_time = int(
            (group_data["max_end_ms"] - duration_ms) // relax_step_ms
        )
        max_start_from_semantic = len(sim_entropy_full[group]) - semantic_points
        max_start_idx = min(max_start_from_time, max_start_from_semantic)

        if max_start_idx < 0:
            continue

        start_idx = random.randint(0, max_start_idx)
        start_time = int(start_idx * relax_step_ms)
        end_time = start_time + duration_ms

        gesture_annots = get_window_of_annotations(
            group_data["eafob"], group, start_time, end_time
        )
        gesture_rate = (
            len(gesture_annots) / (duration_ms / 1000)
        ) * 60

        info_content = group_data["info_content"]
        info_window = info_content[
            (info_content["onset"] * 1000 > start_time)
            & (info_content["onset"] * 1000 < end_time)
        ]["normalised_h"]

        semantic_window = sim_entropy_full[group][
            start_idx:start_idx + semantic_points
        ]

        pseudo_rows.append(
            {
                "group": group,
                "peak_id": observed["peak_id"],
                "relax_duration": observed["relax_duration"],
                "gesture_rate": gesture_rate,
                "relax_info_content": np.nanmean(info_window),
                "mean_semantic_entropy": np.nanmean(semantic_window),
            }
        )

    return pd.DataFrame(pseudo_rows)
In [79]:
relax_test_columns = [
    "gesture_rate",
    "relax_info_content",
    "mean_semantic_entropy",
]

def fit_relaxation_intercept(data, value_col):
    model_data = data[
        ["group", "peak_id", value_col]
    ].dropna().copy()

    model = smf.mixedlm(
        f"{value_col} ~ 1",
        data=model_data,
        groups="group",
        vc_formula={"peak": "0 + C(peak_id)"},
    )
    result = model.fit()
    return result.params["Intercept"]


# Observed mixed-model intercepts
relax_true_coef = {
    value_col: fit_relaxation_intercept(relax_features_df, value_col)
    for value_col in relax_test_columns
}

# Null distributions of the same intercepts
relax_perm_coef = {value_col: [] for value_col in relax_test_columns}

for permut in range(1000):
    relax_pseudo_df = generate_relaxation_pseudo_df()

    for value_col in relax_test_columns:
        try:
            coef = fit_relaxation_intercept(relax_pseudo_df, value_col)
            relax_perm_coef[value_col].append(coef)
        except Exception:
            # Skip model fits that fail to converge or are otherwise invalid.
            relax_perm_coef[value_col].append(np.nan)

def report_relaxation_mixedlm_permutation(value_col, title, x_label):
    observed = relax_true_coef[value_col]
    null_values = np.asarray(relax_perm_coef[value_col], dtype=float)
    null_values = null_values[np.isfinite(null_values)]

    p_lower = (np.sum(null_values <= observed) + 1) / (len(null_values) + 1)
    p_upper = (np.sum(null_values >= observed) + 1) / (len(null_values) + 1)
    p_two_sided = min(1.0, 2 * min(p_lower, p_upper))

    sns.histplot(null_values, kde=True)
    plt.axvline(observed, color="red", label="Observed intercept")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.xlabel(x_label)
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

    print(f"Observed mixed-model intercept: {observed:.6f}")
    print(f"Valid permutations: {len(null_values)}")
    print(f"Lower-tail p: {p_lower:.4f}")
    print(f"Upper-tail p: {p_upper:.4f}")
    print(f"Two-sided p: {p_two_sided:.4f}")


report_relaxation_mixedlm_permutation(
    "gesture_rate",
    "Permutation Test: Gesture Rate During Relaxation Windows",
    "Mixed-model intercept (gestures/minute)",
)

report_relaxation_mixedlm_permutation(
    "relax_info_content",
    "Permutation Test: Information Content During Relaxation Windows",
    "Mixed-model intercept (information content)",
)

report_relaxation_mixedlm_permutation(
    "mean_semantic_entropy",
    "Permutation Test: Semantic Entropy During Relaxation Windows",
    "Mixed-model intercept (semantic entropy)",
)
